questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people move from cities to the countryside
Ways to make noisy cities feel quieter and more relaxing
How to protect your ears at concerts
Why India is the loudest country in the world
questions.why: Georgie says they'll hear about ways to make cities quieter, more relaxing places.

questions.q: How did Neil feel when he heard Georgie's two recordings?
options: Both clips made him feel stressed and tense
Both clips made him feel calm and sleepy
The first relaxed him, but the second stressed him
He couldn't hear any real difference between them
questions.why: He says the first clip made him relaxed, but the second was horrible and stressful.

questions.q: What does the World Health Organisation report, according to Neil?
options: About 2.5 billion people will have hearing loss by 2050
Four billion people will leave cities by 2050
City noise has fallen in recent years
Only aeroplanes cause serious noise problems
questions.why: Neil says the WHO reports that by 2050 around 2.5 billion people will experience hearing loss.

questions.q: How noisy is Mumbai during the day?
options: About 20 decibels
About 50 decibels, like most cities
Just below WHO recommendations
Often 80 decibels, over 20 above WHO advice
questions.why: Neil says daytime noise regularly hits 80 decibels, over 20 higher than WHO recommendations.

questions.q: Why couldn't Chhavi Sachdev cope with the noise when she returned to India?
options: She had got used to quieter places after 12 years
She had developed serious hearing problems
Mumbai had become much louder since she left
She had moved to a flat next to an airport
questions.why: After 12 years in the US and Europe, she says she'd gotten used to lower levels of noise.

questions.q: What gave Charles Montambault the idea for his project?
options: A classical concert he went to in Montreal
Ocean sounds he heard on holiday on some islands
Complaints from people who use his local park
A science study about birdsong in big cities
questions.why: He was inspired to recreate the ocean sounds he heard on holiday in the Magdalen Islands.

questions.q: How did Charles's team play the sounds in the park?
options: Through people's mobile phones
With live musicians
From a large screen in the centre
Through speakers hidden in flower beds
questions.why: They set up the installation as speakers planted in flower beds.

questions.q: Why does Charles call his idea 'counterintuitive'?
options: Because nobody who visited enjoyed the sounds
Because it cost far more than they expected
Because adding sounds made the park feel quieter
Because the sand sounds were hard to record
questions.why: He says you can make a park less noisy by adding calmer sounds, which is not what you'd expect.
